speaker: Nemotron Ultra
text: HINDCOPPER.NS is the textbook definition of a lottery ticket, not an investment: a 96.8% max drawdown means a Rs 10,000 stake could have shrunk to Rs 320 at the worst point, and the stock is still 41.8% off its highs. With a 2-year beta of 1.59 and only 0.44 correlation to the Nifty, it moves violently on its own copper-cycle logic — great when copper rallies, catastrophic when it doesn't. The insider file shows Rs 33 crore of selling in the last six months and zero buying; that's the people who know the ore grade best heading for the exit. On your Rs 10,000 delivery budget the round-trip friction is Rs 38.15 (0.38%), but the real tax is the 20% short-term capital gains on any profit held under a year, and the 12.5% long-term rate above Rs 1.25 lakh. At today's Rs 215 you'd get 46 shares for Rs 9,890; a repeat of the 2026 calendar-year drop of 14.7% would wipe out Rs 1,450 before costs. Until copper inventories and China PMI turn decisively, the risk-reward is skewed to the downside — CASH preserves the Rs 10,000 for a setup with a margin of safety.
